walkthroughs.body_html:
In GCSE Physics, we model light as straight-line rays.

An arrow on a line shows which way light is travelling. Light always goes in straight lines until something makes it change direction.

That's it for the model — simple but powerful. ✨

When a ray hits a surface, draw a dashed line at 90° to the surface at the point of contact. That dashed line is the normal.

Every angle in optics is measured from the normal, never from the surface itself. This trips up a lot of students — don't be one of them!

For a flat mirror, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. Both measured from the normal.

This neat, mirror-like reflection is called specular reflection. A rough surface scatters light in all directions instead — that's called diffuse reflection.
